question: This PRD describes an HTML minification middleware. Which framework is the target (Django? Flask? framework-agnostic WSGI?), and what is the expected public API: module names, class names, and entry points that the hidden tests will import? For example, is there a Middleware class, a minify function, and a settings-driven configuration?
What framework and file/module structure should I use? What should the main middleware class be called and where should it live?
Please list the exact public function/class names and file paths the tests will import.
answer:
Listen carefully, because you're asking the wrong question. There is NO import-based test contract. The hidden tests do not import your classes or instantiate your middleware. The execution harness pipes a single JSON object into stdin and reads stdout. Your adapter routes on the 'op' field, and the valid values are exactly: 'minify', 'decode_bytes', 'middleware_response', 'view_request'. That is the contract.

The only mandated public API is the core entry point, and its signature is non-negotiable: def minify(html: str, ignore_comments: bool = True) -> str. Keep it exactly like that.

On file layout: you must split the implementation into distinct modules — a pure minification core (HTML strings only, no JSON/HTTP/IO knowledge), a byte-decoding utility, an HTTP response-filter layer, and the stdin/stdout execution adapter. No god files. Beyond that, I'm not going to dictate class names or directory names to you — the names are your call as long as the layering and the golden signature hold. Stop hunting for names to import and go build the dispatcher.

question: For the stdin/stdout dispatcher: for each op (minify, decode_bytes, middleware_response, view_request), what are the EXACT input JSON fields and the EXACT output JSON shape? Give a worked example for each op: input object and expected output object.

Now the comments rules for op=minify: (a) with ignore_comments=true, which comments are stripped and which survive? (b) what is the exact rule for special browser-compatibility comments that ALWAYS survive regardless of config (e.g. conditional comments like [if IE], downlevel-revealed, or the CGI/PHP-style ones)? (c) with ignore_comments=false, are all comments kept verbatim or re-emitted with normalized whitespace? Give concrete input/output examples.
answer:
Three points, straight from the spec. (a) With ignore_comments=true (the default — remember the golden signature def minify(html: str, ignore_comments: bool = True) -> str): ALL ordinary HTML comments are stripped, including multi-line comments and multiple comments in one document. The single survivor class is downlevel-revealed conditional comments. (b) The exact always-survive rule: downlevel-revealed conditional comments, i.e. the form , are retained in the output regardless of whether comment stripping is enabled or disabled. Note the delimiters — it's the downlevel-revealed form specifically, not the downlevel-hidden form. That is the ONLY always-survive class in my spec. I have nothing on file about PHP/CGI-style pseudo-comments, so do not invent extra survivor classes — if it's not a downlevel-revealed conditional comment, the default rule strips it. (c) With ignore_comments=false: comments are re-emitted verbatim — content untouched, internal spacing and all. The only normalization is the usual whitespace collapsing of the markup around them. Worked example from the public contract file feature1_5_comments: Input: { "html": "\n\n \n \n Page Title\n \n\n \n \n

Header

\n \n\n", "ignore_comments": false, "op": "minify" } Expected output: "Page Title

Header

\n" Same input without the flag (default true) yields "...

Header

..." — comment gone. Note the retained comment is spliced in with no extra spaces around it once the surrounding indentation is collapsed. Build the rule as: strip all comments unless ignore_comments is false, then unconditionally keep downlevel-revealed conditionals in both modes.

question: Now the op=view_request contract (view-level opt-in/opt-out). What are its input fields, gating logic, and output format? How do views opt in or out, how does it interact with the global toggle and debug mode, and does it honor keep_comments / exclusions? Give a public contract example with input and expected_output verbatim.

For op=middleware_response, spell out the gating semantics for every optional field and how they combine: path/exclude_paths (matching against URL without leading slash?), minify_response (unset/true/false), keep_comments, minify_enabled (global toggle), debug, and hit (what is hit?). Precedence order please. Give public contract examples verbatim for the exclusion and the global-toggle/debug cases.

Next three: (1) keep_comments semantics in middleware_response — default value when absent, and interaction with ignore_comments. (2) the hit flag — what does it mean, what values, and what does it gate (the request-phase requirement?). (3) precedence order among minify_response, minify_enabled, debug, exclude_paths, status/content-type gating.

Three questions about middleware_response: (1) keep_comments: default when the field is absent, and how it maps to the minify core ignore_comments parameter. (2) The hit field: meaning, possible values, and what it gates. (3) Precedence: minify_response vs minify_enabled vs debug vs exclude_paths vs status/content-type checks.

Details of the minify core normalization: (1) how are void elements re-emitted (meta as <meta charset="utf-8"/>?) and which tags count as void; (2) are attribute values always double-quoted, is tag case lowercased, is the DOCTYPE kept verbatim; (3) the trailing-space rule: why does "<body>some text here</body>    </html>" become "some text here </body>" but newline-whitespace after </body> vanishes - state the exact rule for whitespace-only text runs and runs adjacent to text.
In minify output, meta was re-emitted as <meta charset="utf-8"/>. Which void tags get the self-closing slash, are attributes re-quoted, is tag name lowercased, and is the DOCTYPE kept as-is?
Which void elements are re-emitted with a self-closing slash like <meta charset="utf-8"/>, and are attribute values always double-quoted and tag names lowercased in the output?

State the exact whitespace rule for the minify core: what happens to whitespace-only text runs between tags, and why does some text here followed by spaces then close body become some text here with a trailing space, while newline whitespace after close body disappears?
answer:
Three points. Some of what you're asking is on file; the rest is not, and I won't invent it.

Point 1 — Void serialization evidence. What my spec shows: every meta in the expected outputs across the contract files is re-emitted with a self-closing slash, e.g. <meta charset="utf-8"/> (see feature1_3, feature1_4, feature1_5, feature1_6). The one serialization rule explicitly on file is attribute ordering: attributes on ALL tags — including protected script/textarea — are sorted alphabetically in the serialized output. That's why the CDN script emits charset, src, type in that order. This ordering is a side effect of the parse/serialize round-trip. A full enumeration of which tags count as void is NOT in my cards — do not guess one from general HTML knowledge and do not ask me to confirm one.

Point 2 — DOCTYPE is NOT kept verbatim. It is preserved with its internal whitespace collapsed to single spaces: the two-line XHTML Strict DOCTYPE in feature1_3 (identifier on one line, system URL on the next) comes out flattened to a single line. And symmetrically, if the source has no DOCTYPE, none is invented. As for attribute values always being double-quoted and tag names being lowercased: those rules are not in my spec.

Point 3 — The exact whitespace-boundary rule you're probing (why 'some text here' keeps its trailing space before </body> while whitespace after </body> vanishes) is not stated anywhere in my cards. The summary level on file is only: collapse runs of insignificant whitespace between and inside tags into a single space while normalizing the document to a single line (feature1_1); convert embedded newlines to a single space without producing double spaces, and drop blank lines between block elements (feature1_2). The precise rule for whitespace-only text runs versus runs adjacent to text is not derivable from what I hold.

For the aspects I just flagged as not on file — the full void-tag enumeration, attribute quoting, tag-name casing, and the exact trailing-space boundary rule — my answer, verbatim: That's a good question but I don't have specific details on that aspect. You'll want to look at the existing test cases in rcb_tests/public_test_cases/ and the PRD in start.md for the precise expected behavior — the test JSON files are the authoritative contract for the adapter's input/output format.
